author: Income Machine
title: 4 International Dividend Stocks To Consider
text:
Many authors I follow on Seeking Alpha are exclusively concentrated in domestic equities. Portfolios may be diverse by sector , but they are infrequently diverse geographically. The lion’s share of companies these investors select are multinationals with expansive business in other parts of the world but domiciled in the United States. Some examples are: McDonald’s (NYSE: MCD ), Exxon Mobil (NYSE: XOM ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Nike (NYSE: NKE ), and Visa (NYSE: V ). (Great companies all, for the record.)
I can understand why. With the recent Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 , these companies are poised to juice their profits through lower tax rates. And that will result in enormous buybacks and dividend raises as businesses share the spoils with shareholders. Historically, the American exchanges are indisputably superior and investors are wise to presume that past is prelude and good times will continue moving forward.
I hold many American multinational companies in my portfolio and for the most part I intend to never sell any of them.
Having said that, it is my belief that the recent exuberance in domestic markets has somewhat muted prospective returns for the immediate future and I find the most compelling opportunities abroad.
For this column’s purpose, I’d like to turn the arrangement – companies domiciled domestically with business abroad – on its head and focus on international companies that do business in the United States. Below I share 4 companies I own in a variety of sectors that I believe offer lucrative opportunities today for those seeking to expand their horizons.
Maersk ( OTCPK:AMKBY ) – Shipping (Denmark) 1.8% Yield Chances are if you live anywhere near a port or the coasts you’ve seen containers on the highways bearing the Maersk name:
A.P. Moller- Maersk is the global integrator of container logistics , and the world’s largest shipping company with over 4M TEU containers moved between Europe and Asia. Many economists use Maersk as a barometer for the health of the world economy. As the world’s largest shipper, Maersk shares often track the freight indexes as the market (like oil) is cyclical, fluctuating sharply like the choppy waters as supply and demand are often out-of-balance.
The company is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark and has a separate U.S. subsidiary unit named Maersk Line, Limited which operates 18 ships with a subsidy from the United States military through the Maritime Security Program.
Maersk is also a dividend paying stock delivering one payout per year. The present yield is a paltry 1.8% at today’s share price of $6.91. However, payouts can vary significantly from year-to-year as demonstrated below:
Image from Charles Schwab
The payout could be halved next year, or it could double. Maersk is in the midst of a turbulent few years as shares are retreating back toward their 5-year low. The global shipping business remains overbuilt and tariffs have further spooked investors. But this is a notoriously cyclical market and despite recent operating losses, the pendulum typically swings pretty hard the opposite direction.
Despite these challenges, the company’s revenue increased 30% due to its acquisition of Hamburg Sud. Maersk also recently sold its oil division to Total (NYSE: TOT ) to focus on its logistics and shipping empire. This sale decreased debt and allowed Maersk to maintain its investment grade rating of BBB from Standard & Poor’s .
Shares can be bought OTC as an ADR and are subject to international tax withholding. I plan to add to my existing stake if shares linger in the $6.00 range and I view this as a long-term hold.
Suez ( OTCPK:SZEVY ) – Utility (France) 5.7% Yield
Suez is a global leader in resource management , providing water and waste recycling services to over 7.5M people in the United States and Canada alone. The company is French, and before I hear the cacophony of groans, hear me out. After all, the two French companies I’ve written about on Seeking Alpha, Veolia ( OTCPK:VEOEY ) and Electricite de France ( OTCPK:ECIFY ), found here and here have returned 32% and 57% respectively in just over a year excluding dividends .
France gets a bad rap, but with centrist and free-trade proponent Emmanuel Macron at the helm , I believe the future is brighter than ever. Laser-focused on sustainability and aligned with responsible investing, this is an easy business to support as a water utility operating in a monopolistic environment.
And as General Electric (NYSE: GE ) disintegrates and bids farewell to the DJIA, Suez is a beneficiary as it absorbed the GE Water business providing another avenue for growth. Suez is active in 5 continents with over 90,000 employees. They earned over $16B in revenue in 2017
Suez’s share price has suffered as it is now also declining toward its 5-year low:
Chart from Charles Schwab
However the financials tell a different story. In the first quarter of this year , revenue increased 9.1% with an EBIT margin of 7.7%. Net debt to EBITDA increased to 3.3x due to the GE Water acquisition but Suez is committed to keeping leverage in check. The credit markets must like what they see as Suez issued a hybrid bond at a cheap 2.875% to help finance that GE Water acquisition.
Suez, like most utilities, is committed to rewarding shareholders through generous dividends. They currently have a consistent payment of €0.65 which, subject to currency fluctuations, equates to about $.38/share for the ADR shares. At today’s price of $6.57 that’s equivalent to a 5.7% yield.
Shares can be bought OTC as an ADR and are subject to international tax withholding. My cost basis is about $7 but I may average down if the price continues to decline.
Skanska ( OTCPK:SKBSY ) – Construction & Engineering (Sweden) 5.54% Yield
Admittedly, I was too early initiating a position in Skanska and am currently underwater by about 17%. I previously wrote in depth about the company here and here . Skanska is a Swedish construction company with an American division that works on airports, bridges, tunnels, medical centers, and other infrastructure projects. Here’s a look at the Q2 order bookings, you’ll note the medical facility in Hollywood, California :
Skanska Order Bookings
Skanska is becoming much more selective during the bidding process to ensure they only tackle projects where they can capture a reasonable profit. While numeric values of contracts are large, margins are slim and small snags can cause major delays which impede timelines and ultimately, profits. Above you can note the investment-grade credit worthiness of the clients which range from various municipalities to universities.
The American footprint is significant as Skanska’s projects include: the MetLife Stadium where the Giants and Jets play, LaGuardia Airport, the Alaskan Way Viaduct in Seattle, the Carolina Bays Parkway in South Carolina, to the Elizabeth River Tunnels in Norfolk, Virginia. Chances are you’ve encountered a Skanska project or two traveling in the United States.
Despite a revenue increase of 8% in Q1 , shares have continued to sell off as Skanska takes restructuring charges which undermined its operating income and cash flow. It is my belief that the industry has strong tailwinds with or without a federal infrastructure stimulus and Skanska is poised to benefit from the many projects long overdue. With the increased focus of quality over quantity, Skanska has repurposed its efforts in securing the most lucrative contracts and avoiding uber-competitive bids and riskier proposals.
At today’s pricing in the $17.50 range, investors can lock up a high-yield of 5.5%. Skanska is committed to rewarding shareholders as demonstrated below:
Image
The stock trades within shouting distance of its 5-year low. Shares can be bought OTC as an ADR and are subject to international tax withholding. My cost basis is about $20.90 and I have averaged down as the price continues to decline. The spread between the bid and ask is significant and liquidity is poor. But for a buy-and-hold dividend investor this is a solid long-term hold.
Transurban ( OTCPK:TRAUF ) – Industrials (Australia) 4.63% Yield
Anyone unlucky enough to live in the southern metropolitan region of Washington D.C. has inured themselves to congestion. There are three things for certain there: death, taxes, and traffic on the interstate. Transurban was tasked to alleviate the latter by building toll lanes connecting the outer suburbs to Washington. That project was a demonstrable success and Transurban has committed to extending the project down to Fredericksburg:
FY 18 Half-Year Results
As you may have guessed, Transurban manages and develops urban toll roads in Australia and North America. While much of their business remains in Australia in places like Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Queensland, management is pursuing opportunities elsewhere in the United States on the heels of the work done in the mid-Atlantic. Norfolk and Virginia Beach seem like a natural fit as both localities are paralyzed by traffic and its close proximity to the capitol area.
Transurban is a reputable partner with a cheap cost of capital of 4.3%. S&P rates their corporate debt at BBB+ and Fitch has an A- rating. Revenues have ticked up y/y and EBITDA increased 11.6% from 2017-2018:
Proportional Results slide #47
Toll revenue growth was almost 18% y/y in Washington and the company forecasts numerous tailwinds for the industry to include fast-growing populations, an 86% freight increase by 2031, along with an $800B infrastructure backlog in Australia. Like Skanska, Transurban is earning its stripes in the United States and ultimately I believe they will secure more contracts as cities grind to a halt as millennials flock to urban centers for jobs.
Dividend investors can also rejoice as the growth has been nothing short of stellar:
Image
I have only begun layering into my position with this company. My brother lives in Washington and we visit each other frequently and we have no reasonable alternative than to use I-95 which is Transurban’s bread and butter. This is a business I only regret not buying into sooner.
Unlike the other companies listed above, this stock is trading somewhat near its 52-week high. Shares can be bought OTC and are subject to international tax withholding. My cost basis is about $9.00 and plan to average into the name within the next year. The spread between the bid and ask is significant and liquidity is poor. But for a buy-and-hold dividend investor this is a solid long-term hold.
Conclusion: The United States remains a premier destination to invest. American multinational companies have minted many a millionaire over the years and it would be foolish to dissuade anyone from investing domestically or believing that will change in the future. I certainly don’t.
But it is my belief that investors can also benefit from the relative cheaper valuations abroad from select companies. These organizations are not as unfamiliar as they may seem since each of the businesses listed above have expansive operations in the United States. And I always prefer to invest in companies that I know and buy/use . The theory goes: If I have to pay a toll, I may as well collect some of it back at the end of the month/quarter via dividend.
I extrapolate that strategy by owning shares of my cellular carrier, my smart phone manufacturer, my local utility, etc.
My portfolio is host to many international companies, perhaps too many, but I believe in the power of diversification and if you pick your spots it can lead to outperformance.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AMKBY, SZEVY, SKBSY, TRAUF, ECIFY, VEOEY.
